units.source_text: 古歌：“惯说人生苦，常言世智辛。

en.t: An old poem says: "People are used to saying that life is bitter, and often say that worldly wisdom is harsh.

units.source_text: 山梨花似锦，何处可藏身？”

en.t: The flowers of Yamanashi are like brocade; where can one hide oneself?"
This appears in Kokin Waka Rokujō.

units.source_text: “山梨”是地名，其发音与“无山”同，

en.t: "Yamanashi" is a place name, and its pronunciation is the same as "no mountain,"

units.source_text: 诗意双关，谓无山可藏身也。

en.t: so the poem makes a pun, meaning that there is no mountain where one can hide.
